subject: Inference session stall — Customer overview, timeline, and verification plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acmecloud.com>, support@acmecloud.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Preliminary readout — inference session stall and immediate mitigations

Hi Elena / Acme team,

Thank you again for bearing with us this morning. I wanted to share a concise preliminary readout from our side and the immediate mitigations we applied while our engineers completed the deeper analysis.

Summary (brief)
- Impact: A subset of inference sessions for your account experienced stalls while the model KV cache eviction and prefix routing logic interacted unexpectedly under high concurrent short-sequence load. Impacted requests saw token generation stalls for ~4-18s before automatic retries completed.
- Window: 2026-10-24 07:03 - 07:56 UTC (we attach an exported timeline).
- Scope: ~0.7% of total requests from your dedicated pool; primarily short-turnaround chat sessions.

Immediate mitigations implemented (already active)
- Disabled aggressive KV pre-eviction heuristic for your pool (falls back to conservative policy).
- Enabled short-request isolation routing to spare low-latency lanes from batch-induced stalls.
- Increased retry budget for stalled token streams to prevent client-visible partial outputs.

Next steps from Redwood (this week)
1) Full RCA & customer-facing summary (draft attached) — Jonas (today)
2) Controlled rollout of kernel-fix to reduce pre-eviction races (canary Tuesday) — Engineering
3) Verification run with your test prompts and joint acceptance — schedule with Marissa

Attachments: acme_rca_v1.pdf (draft), timeline_events.csv (event export)

I know any disruption to your flows is unacceptable — we own this and will provide concrete timelines for the fix and verification artifacts. I'll follow up with the full customer-facing RCA and a verification checklist by tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Jonas,

2) For the canary kernel-fix, what is the rollback plan if we see regression in latency for long-sequence workloads?

We appreciate the clear ownership. Please include those points in the final document. Also, can we get the verification checklist ahead of the joint run so we can prepare our test harness?

Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Final customer RCA & verification plan (attached)

Elena / Acme team,

Per your note, attached is the customer-facing RCA (acme_rca_v1.pdf), a machine-exported timeline (timeline_events.csv), and an initial verification checklist (verification_checklist.xlsx). Below is a concise summary that highlights the items you asked about.

Executive summary
- Root cause: A race between our KV cache pre-eviction heuristic and the prefix-based routing optimization for short sequence requests. Under a burst of concurrent short sessions, certain cache entries were evicted while in-use pointers remained referenced by the runtime's tokenization boundaries, causing the runtime to pause to reconcile and rehydrate state. This manifested as stalls (token generation pauses) for impacted requests.
- Visible outcome: In retries we either re-streamed the response from start or resumed after rehydration; in <0.1% of impacted sessions we observed truncated outputs that required manual re-run by the client. We identified 12 truncated-response events in your account during the window.

Timeline (high level)
- 2026-10-24 07:03 UTC — first anomalous increase in stalled token generation for short sessions
- 2026-10-24 07:10 UTC — automated detection alerted on elevated stall rate; on-call investigation begins
- 2026-10-24 07:22 UTC — deployed temporary mitigation (conservative eviction policy) to your dedicated pool
- 2026-10-24 07:37 UTC — routing isolation enabled for short requests; stall rate dropped sharply
- 2026-10-24 07:56 UTC — incident considered mitigated; monitoring shows normal baselines

Answers to your clarifications
1) Partial/truncated outputs: We found 12 truncated-response incidents attributable to retries during rehydration. We recommend notifying affected end-users where you have deterministic logs; we can provide a CSV of the request IDs for targeted outreach.
2) Canary rollback plan: The kernel-fix will be deployed to a canary subset (5% of capacity) with automated rollback triggers: 1) >10% latency regression for long-sequence requests vs baseline for 10 minutes, or 2) any increase in stall rate >2x baseline. Rollback is immediate and manual intervention will be used only if automation does not trigger.

Action items & schedule
- (A1) Engineering to ship kernel-fix to canary (target: Tue 2026-10-27 02:00 UTC) — Rishi
- (A2) Joint verification run using your test harness and the attached checklist (suggested window: Wed 2026-10-28 14:00-15:30 UTC) — Marissa to coordinate
- (A3) CSV of impacted request IDs for targeted user notification (by EOD Mon 2026-10-26) — Jonas
- (A4) Post-canary monitoring window & rollback decision (48 hours after canary) — Engineering

Attachments: acme_rca_v1.pdf, timeline_events.csv, verification_checklist.xlsx

If you want, Marissa and I can run a 30-minute readout with your SREs to walk through the checklist and monitoring playbook.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber

Subject: Re: Final customer RCA & verification plan (attached)

Elena / Jonas,

Thanks for the thorough RCA, Jonas — and Elena, thanks for the quick questions.

Logistics for verification run
- Proposed joint window: Wed 2026-10-28 14:00-15:30 UTC (we'll reserve the dedicated pool and run the checklist end-to-end). Please confirm test account credentials and an SRE point-of-contact.
- Acceptance criteria: no stalls >1s for short-session workload in a 30-minute steady-state run and zero truncated outputs in the verification suite.
- Evidence: We'll produce an artifacts bundle (logs, rehydration traces, token latency histograms) and upload to the shared Drive link.

SLA / credits note (operational)
- We've flagged this incident for the account review; if you opt for formal SLA credit we will prepare the calculation and include it in the post-verification packet. We do not expect this to impact the canary schedule.

I'll coordinate the calendar invite and the shared Drive folder. Jonas — can you upload the CSV of impacted request IDs by EOD so Acme can start outreach?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com
